proposed_title: DeepMind describes a double-blind proprietary-model evaluation pilot
what_happened: Fresh Cloud GETs retrieved Google DeepMind's exact 27 August 2026 announcement and its linked technical report. DeepMind says its pilot uses cryptographically secured environments so model providers and evaluators do not see each other's protected assets. A separate current arXiv record supplies an independent technical trail about efficient software-agent evaluation, but does not validate DeepMind's system.
key_facts: COMPANY_CLAIM: DeepMind calls the pilot the first double-blind AI evaluation approach and says it can protect proprietary models and evaluation data.
FACT: the announcement links a technical report that was retrieved in this run.

ABSTRACT_ONLY: arXiv 2609.01603 proposes trajectory-aware sampling and ability estimation for software-agent benchmarks and reports results across four benchmarks; this packet inspected only its abstract record.
UNKNOWN: no independent replication, security audit or deployed evaluation result for DeepMind's pilot was retrieved.

primary_sources.attribution: Google DeepMind announcement by William Isaac, Sol Messing and Kristian Lum
primary_sources.claim_supported: DeepMind's description, novelty claim and intended safeguards for its pilot

primary_sources.attribution: Technical report linked by Google DeepMind
primary_sources.claim_supported: The company's documented methodology and findings for the pilot
primary_sources.independence: Company technical document; separate detail, not independent corroboration

independent_sources.attribution: Duan et al. abstract record for Efficient SWE Agent Benchmarking via Trajectory-Aware Evaluation
independent_sources.claim_supported: A current independent technical approach to estimating software-agent benchmark performance
independent_sources.independence: Independent author team and different method; not peer reviewed and not a test of DeepMind's pilot

contradictory_evidence: A company-defined security design is not evidence that an independent evaluator has audited the implementation.
The arXiv paper addresses evaluation efficiency, not double-blind confidentiality, so it cannot corroborate DeepMind's claims.
uncertainty: The announcement and linked report establish what DeepMind describes; novelty, security and performance remain unverified independently.
context: Proprietary-model evaluations can expose model weights or secret tests; this packet separates the proposed mechanism from proof that it works.
why_it_matters: If independently validated, protected evaluation infrastructure could let outside evaluators test closed models without either side disclosing sensitive assets.
strategic_angle: BRIEF the pilot as a COMPANY_CLAIM; do not publish an evaluation verdict.
